book.totem.locksmith_manual.title: Locksmith Method Guide
book.totem.locksmith_manual.page.1:
GETTING STARTED

Locksmith protects Chests, Trapped Chests, Barrels, double chests, and fixed-Hopper-connected storage. Start by crafting one Padlock.
book.totem.locksmith_manual.page.2:
PADLOCK RECIPE

Five Iron Ingots and one Iron Nugget make one Padlock. The next page shows the live server recipe.
book.totem.locksmith_manual.page.3:
APPLYING A LOCK

Hold the Padlock and use it on a Chest, Trapped Chest, or Barrel. The first container becomes the root. Loaded fixed Hoppers and supported containers in that network share the same lock.
book.totem.locksmith_manual.page.4:
KEY BLANKS

Craft Key Blanks before issuing physical keys. Five Iron Nuggets make two blanks. The next page shows the exact arrangement.
book.totem.locksmith_manual.page.5:
ISSUING A KEY

Look at a locked container or member Hopper within 6 blocks, hold a Key Blank in either hand, then run /locksmith key bind. The server consumes one blank and issues a Bound Key tied to that lock and key generation.
book.totem.locksmith_manual.page.6:
USING KEYS

A valid Bound Key grants access only while it remains in the main hand or offhand. Keys can be revoked or rotated. Blocked players stay denied even if they hold a valid physical key.
book.totem.locksmith_manual.page.7:
ACCESS ROLES

Owner has full control. Managers maintain users and ordinary keys. Users gain access when the selected mode allows it. Blocked overrides users, friends, public access, and keys.
book.totem.locksmith_manual.page.8:
NETWORKS & AUTOMATION

Internal Hopper transfers inside one lock continue normally. Boundary INSERT and EXTRACT follow the lock's automation policy. Breaking a middle Hopper leaves only the root component locked.
book.totem.locksmith_manual.page.9:
REMOVAL & RECYCLING

Run /locksmith remove while targeting the network to return one Padlock. A Bound Key can be placed by itself in crafting to recycle it into one Key Blank. Non-owner container breaks follow normal Minecraft rules and may emit an audit event.
